page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with short marginal notes in the left margin at lines 7 and 8 and small marks in the right margin. Running head at top centre. Catchword at bottom right. No page number.

main_text.p: §. Salus populi Principi suprema lex esto: ut ni-mirum
Beata civium vita sit religione sancta, virtute honesta, gloria ampla, copiis locuples, opibus firma.
Tyranni natura, boni Principis moribus ę diametro contraria.
§. Princeps νομοθέτης esto justus, & acer νομοφύ-λαξ: in quo utroque imitandus Deus.
Altera hic Regis & tyranni differentia ostenditur.
7. lenitate:Sit piger ad poenas Princeps, ad praemia velox.
De Republica bene meritos, non defraudandos esse debitis honoribus; sed potius ad sublimiores dignitates evehedos.
In poenis irrogandis qualem se gerere debeat bonus Princeps, & quo modo procedere.
Rex à tyranno qualiter hic quoq; differat.
§. fide:Princeps fidei memor esto tenaxq;: utpote quae Societatis humanae vinculum est adamantinum:
Principes inprimis decet: qui idcirco nihil temere promittere debent.
Fidem hosti quoque esse servandam: idque potissimum ob perfidiae & perjurii poenam divinam.

page.notes: The section numbers 5 to 8 are shown as printed; the marks before 5, 6 and 8 look like section signs (§) and may be misread. The Greek words νομοθέτης and νομοφύλαξ are read from a small and worn print and are not certain. The hyphen in "ni-mirum" is faint and may be a comma. The sign after "moribus" is unclear and may be an abbreviation of "et". Marks in the right margin (a small asterisk after "vulpina", and slashes near the Greek line and near "Fides") may be printer's marks or show-through and are not transcribed. The left-margin catchword marks look like printed note references and are kept as notes.
